Logo, logotype & app icon

Three marks, one decision: how much room is there, and does the reader already know what Raqt is. Two of the three are alpha masks painted by a token, so they invert with the mode on their own — there is no light-mode file to keep in sync.

Logo

The full lockup — wordmark over the tagline. The only mark that says what Raqt is.

First contact: marketing, the login screen, a footer, a printed draw sheet.

Logotype

Wordmark alone. Reads at a third of the height because nothing small has to survive.

In-product chrome: app header, nav bar, anywhere the reader is already inside Raqt.

App icon

The R alone, on its own opaque ground. A picture, not a mask.

Home screen, favicon, avatar — any square the platform draws for you.

Dark — the default

Both painted --color-foreground — #EAF5EF here. The mark is never the green: primary marks the one thing to do next, and a logo is not an action.

Light

Both painted --color-foreground — #071410 here. Nothing swapped the file — foreground changed and the mask followed.

Size floor — this is what picks the mark

The binding constraint on the logo is never RAQT — it is the tagline, set at roughly a fifth of the wordmark's height. Below about 160px wide it stops resolving and the lockup becomes a wordmark with a grey smudge under it, which is worse than a wordmark. That is the whole reason the logotype exists: it is the same mark with the fragile part removed, so it holds down to about 90px. Below that, the icon.

Clear space

Both files are cropped tight — there is no built-in margin. logo.png's ink runs to the canvas edge on three sides and logotype.png's on two; set either one flush in a header and the glyphs touch the box. Clear space is the layout's job, always, and it is not something a designer can eyeball from the asset.

Proposed, not yet ratified: clear space on all four sides equal to the cap height of the wordmark, as drawn here. Nothing sets in it, including the edge of the surface the mark sits on. Replace this with the real rule if the brand has one.

Open question — the charcoal. The app icon is #2B2F30, a neutral. The system's near-black is #071410, green-tinted ink, and that is what the masked marks are painted in light mode. They read as the same colour alone and visibly differ side by side. No token names #2B2F30, so as it stands it is an undocumented value — which by §4 is a contract change, not something to inline. Either the icon moves onto the ink, or the charcoal earns a brand-* primitive.

assets/brand/icon.png also carries JPEG bytes under a .png name. Nothing is broken — the emitter declares it image/jpeg — but the name is wrong.

Don't

Not in the green
Not at reduced contrast
Never stretched
Not below its floor
